visual_action: The video starts with a black-and-white clip of a man in a cap walking down the stairs of an airplane. It then transitions to a montage of color clips of Donald Trump: taking a selfie with a woman at a factory, speaking at a rally, signing a document while surrounded by people, and walking down a red carpet at a port with a large ship in the background.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: Donald Trump is shown in multiple positive clips throughout the video montage and is the subject of the on-screen text comparing tax returns.

cast.name: Joe Biden
cast.evidence: The video opens with a clip of a man deplaning, juxtaposed with text about 'Tax returns last year'. Given the account (@whitehouse) and the comparison to Trump, this figure is meant to represent the current president, Joe Biden.

cast.name: IRS
cast.evidence: The on-screen text cites 'IRS data' and mentions the 'IRS deadline'.

on_screen_text.text: Average tax refund is up $350 compared to last year as IRS deadline approaches
Average tax refund up nearly 11% from a year ago, IRS data shows

spoken_summary: The audio consists of lyrics from the song 'Young Dumb & Broke' by Khalid, specifically the line 'Young, dumb, broke high school kids'.
audio_music: The song 'Young Dumb & Broke' by Khalid plays throughout the video. It is an upbeat, contemporary pop/R&B track that gives the video a modern, almost 'vibey' feel.
editing_pacing: The video is a fast-paced montage with quick cuts between different short clips, each featuring a text overlay.
cultural_references: The song 'Young Dumb & Broke' by recording artist Khalid is used as the soundtrack.
central_claim: Tax refunds for average Americans were significantly higher during the Trump administration compared to the subsequent year under the current administration.
intended_effect: To persuade viewers that they were financially better off under Donald Trump's economic policies and to generate support for his leadership.
